compactRecord.rs: Veliki Alan sits in Northern Velebit National Park with Adriatic panoramas from 1,414 m, a mountain hut, and a historically striking abandoned cable car built by Goli Otok political prisoners, but remains niche and virtually unknown outside Croatia.
compactRecord.td: A scenic 1,414 m pass inside Northern Velebit National Park with sweeping Adriatic views on the climb from the port of Jablanac. The summit area holds a mountain hut and an eerie abandoned timber ropeway once built by political prisoners of the Goli Otok gulag.

compactRecord.rs: Modest Velebit pass on Croatian state road D25 linking Lika to the Adriatic; scenic karst mountain landscape with a stone-staired hilltop viewpoint from which the Apennines and Italian coast are visible on clear days, but negligible international profile or cycling/touring fame.
compactRecord.td: Oštarijska vrata (928 m) crosses the Velebit range on road D25, connecting Gospić to the Adriatic port of Karlobag. Thirty-eight stone steps climb to a nearby highpoint with a remarkable clear-day view of the Italian coast and Apennines; the winding descent to the sea is the drive's highlight.

compactRecord.rs: Vratnik offers a genuinely beautiful panorama of Kvarner Bay and Dalmatian islands (Krk, Rab) from the Velebit edge, but is a low-elevation stub-article pass with no famous summit facilities, modest hairpin character, and purely regional Croatian recognition.
compactRecord.td: Vratnik (698 m) is a Velebit pass above the historic town of Senj, rewarding drivers with sweeping views over Kvarner Bay and the Dalmatian islands. Historically important as a coastal–inland crossing, it remains a quiet regional route with no dedicated summit attractions.
